title: github - How do I reverse a commit in git? - Stack Overflow
snippet: If you want to revert the last commit, you can use git revert head. head refers to the most recent commit in your branch. The reason you use head~1 when using reset is that you are telling Git to "remove all changes in the commits after" (reset --hard) "the commit one before head" (head~1).

title: How To Revert A Commit With Git Revert? - GeeksforGeeks
snippet: Jul 30, 2025 · When working with Git, it is common to make a commit that later needs to be undone whether due to a bug, accidental changes, or a mistake in the workflow. Instead of deleting or rewriting history, Git provides the git revert command to safely undo a specific commit by creating a new one that reverses its changes.
